newsitem.title: UK: U.S. rates overshadow markets, bourses skid.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rates overshadow markets, bourses skid.

text.p: Major European bourses closed sharply lower on Monday worried about credit tightening at a U.S. monetary policy-making meeting this week and bruised by a tumbling Wall Street.
The meeting of the U.S. Federal Open Markets Committee (FOMC) on Tuesday was overshadowing both stock and currency markets.
"People will just be sitting tight, desperately keen to keep out of trouble," said stock trader.

In New York the Dow Jones Industrial Average tumbled more than three quarters of a percent or about 50 points within minutes of opening. Investors were worried that an increase in interest rates could take a bite out of the U.S. economy, hurting 1997 earnings. Wall Street had recovered slightly by the time European markets closed.

"It's getting sloppy out there. The light volume says you should attach a little less importance to it ... but there's no question that people are worried," said First Albany chief investment officer Hugh Johnson.

Leading London stocks closed down 1.12 percent at 3919.7 but dealers said trading volume was relatively light. On Friday, the blue chip FTSE 100 index had closed down 10 points after hitting an intraday peak of 3,994.1 -- just short of the psychologically-important 4,000 level.
In Frankfurt, German shares ended bourse trade down nearly one percent, slipping on profit-taking after recent sharp gains and on uncertainity ahead of Tuesday's Fed rate decision.
The 30-share DAX ended bourse trade down 19.06 points at 2,627.04.

And on the Paris bourse shares also closed lower pummelled by the early 50-point fall in the Dow and by profit-taking earlier in the day. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 12.37 points or 0.59 percent at 2,067.09.
Italy's stock exchange failed to open due to serious technical problems for the first time since the Milan bourse started its move towards screen-based share trading in 1991.
On the currency markets, the dollar closed European trading slightly lower, dragged down by squaring of long positions and the sharp early stock tumble on Wall Street, dealers said.

Selling pressure on the dollar was exacerbated by thin trading and the wait-and-see attitude many players adopted ahead of Tuesday's FOMC. "In a market like that a few big trades can have quite a big effect, so the dollar came under a bit of pressure this afternoon," said Pat Magill, head of the corporate desk at Daiwa Europe in London.
Against European currencies, particularly the French franc, the mark lost ground in early trading following the weekend European finance ministers' meeting in Dublin.
The gathering pace of Europe's drive towards monetary union, not only put pressure on the mark but also lifted the European currency unit to 21-month high.
On Friday the mark slipped to a two-month low against the franc. It weakened further to a 3-1/2 month low early on Monday to around 3.3801 francs before recovering later in the day.

"Having ridden on the crest of a wave of optimism about EMU prospects, foreign exchange markets will shift their attention back to monetary policy this week, with the key event clearly being the FOMC meeting on Tuesday," said Klaus Baader, currency economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
The markets were counting on 0.25 percent U.S. rate rise and only a surprise 0.5 percent increase would shake the dollar out of its well-trodden ranges, analysts said.
On the precious metals market, platinum fixed at the lowest level for nearly 2-1/2 years as weakness in silver pressured the rest of the precious metals market.
Platinum fixed at $386.50 per ounce, the lowest since April 20, 1994, compared with $387.25 on Friday afternoon.
Heavy selling by US investment funds and other speculators last week shaved 13 cents off the price of spot silver, pushing it below the key $5.00 per ounce level.
CURRENCIES AT 1530 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5120 marks and 109.85 yen compared with 1.5141 marks and 109.76 yen in Europe late on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares closed 44.4 points down at 3,919.7.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index closed 12.37 points down at 2,067.09.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed down 19.06 at 2,627.04. PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $381.25 compared with a close of $381.75 in London on Friday. Silver ended barely changed, up one cent at $4.88 after Friday's tumble to fresh 18-month lows.
